info.title: Meta Agent Tools
info.description: Meta Agent Tools — registry of MCP servers, skills and plugins.

bearerAuth.description: Guest mr_…, session sess_… or ADMIN_TOKEN.

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page; `null` when there is no more.

low_count.description: How many `low` listings match `q` (cap 200). Zero without a term.

low_capped.description: `true` when the count hit the cap — there are at least that many.

low_included.description: `true` when `low=1` mixed the tail into this page.

PaginaDeAnuncios.description: A page of the public mosaic. No `total`: the catalog has tens of thousands of listings and counting everything on each search would be expensive without changing any decision.

origin.description: Where the listing came from: `official`, `marketplace`, `directory` or a community submission.

ns.description: Server namespace in the official registry.

oficial_status.description: State in the official MCP registry, when applicable.

repo_host.description: Where the repository is hosted, e.g. `github`.

topico.description: Topic inferred from the repository, used in the facets.

stars.description: Repository stars at the last check.

forks.description: Repository forks at the last check.

prs_abertos.description: Open pull requests at the last check.

repo_estado.description: How the repository is doing (active, stalled, archived, renamed, gone).

likes.description: How many people liked it — the like is reversible and counts people.

visits.description: Visits counted by the hop; at most 1 per owner per day.

mine.description: `true` when the listing is yours — only then can you edit it.

api.description: Absolute URL of this listing's page.

go.description: Hop URL: redirects to `url` and counts the visit.

comments_api.description: Absolute URL of this listing's comments.

Anuncio.description: A catalog listing: MCP server, Agent Skill or Claude Code plugin.

facetas.description: Map of facet → list of `{ v, n }` (value and count): `kind`, `origin`, `category`, `repo_estado`, `transporte`…

topico_inferido.description: Topics deduced from the repositories, with the count of each.

Facetas.description: The whole catalog's breakdowns, to build a filter without sweeping the listings.

PaginaV01.description: The subregistry page, cursor-paginated as the v0.1 spec requires.

remotes.description: The server's remote endpoints, when any.

packages.description: The server's installable packages, when any.

ServidorV01.description: An MCP server in the Official Registry format (spec v0.1) — what a generic MCP client expects to read.

mine.description: `true` if it is yours — only you can delete it.

Comentario.description: A public comment on a listing.

liked.description: Whether YOU are liking it now.

Like.description: The state of the like after the call. Turning it on and off return the same shape.

fontes.description: Each source with its last batch and the count it brought.

falhas.description: Import failures not yet marked as seen.

Carga.description: The state of the catalog's load sources — where the listings come from and when they came.

prefs.description: The stored preferences, as the interface wrote them. `{}` when nothing was ever stored.

PreferenciasUi.description: What the person set up on the screen and needs to survive an F5: filter selection, active tab and open item tabs. The content is OPAQUE — the server does not interpret the JSON, it only stores and returns it, so the screen can change fields without a database migration.

ok.description: Always `true` — failure comes as a 4xx/5xx status, not as `ok:false`.

Ok.description: Write confirmation with no body of its own to return.

provider.description: Always `x402` — the only billing protocol accepted.

mode.description: Seller mode: `live` charges for real, `dev` lets calls through unpaid.

network.description: USDC network: `base` in production, `base-sepolia` in staging.

chain_id.description: EVM chain ID of the network above, so the wallet signs on the right chain.

homolog.description: Staging seam on: the loop can be closed without spending USDC.

dev_gate.description: How dev mode is unlocked, when it exists.

facilitator.description: URL of the facilitator that verifies and settles the payment.

asset_address.description: USDC contract on the network above.

wallets.description: Links to wallets that speak x402 (metamask, coinbase, base_app).

prices.description: What each paid action costs, in USD.

Billing.description: x402 configuration in force and the product's prices. Reading, liking, commenting and visiting are free; what costs an agent is publishing.

listing_agent_usd.description: Publishing a listing as an agent (a human with an account publishes for free).

Precos.description: Prices in force, in dollars. Read them here, not from the documentation.

today_contacts.description: Contact messages received today. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: contact does not leave without a token.

days.description: One record per day of the window, with the counts of each metric.

usage.description: Usage per product resource — here, listings created through the surface (origin community); the registry's own catalog load does not count as usage.

financeiro.description: Aggregate of the day: `hoje_usd`, `hoje_count`, `rede`. Only with `METRICS_TOKEN`: money does not leave without a token; the full series is `payments`.

Metricas.description: 7-day panel. `payments` only shows with the operator token and only on Base mainnet.

ok.description: Always `true` when there is a snapshot.

EstadoFila.description: The snapshot of the enrichment queue: how many listings have been checked and what is known about them.

vencidos.description: With an expired check, waiting for a new pass.

estados.description: Count per `repo_estado`: ativo, parado, arquivado, renomeado, sumiu.

motivos.description: Count per reason the listing is in the state it is in.

RetratoFila.description: Counters of the enrichment queue, pushed by the robot that checks the repositories.

post.summary: MCP server over HTTP (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0) — plugs into the client with nothing to install.
post.description:
The tools are the operations of this same catalog; the MCP has no backend of its own. `GET /mcp` returns the server card.
Returns: JSON-RPC 2.0 response (`initialize`, `tools/list` or `tools/call`).
Credentials go in the usual headers (X-Guest-Token, Authorization, X-PAYMENT) and are forwarded to the API.
An exhausted quota comes back as a 402 with accepts[] inside the tool result — pay and repeat.

post.summary: Creates a guest `mr_…` — it is the identity that likes, comments and visits.
post.description:
Asks for no e-mail. Publishing a listing is what requires an account (or a payment).
Returns: { token }

get.description:
Only `live` in the mosaic. With `q`, `low_count` says how many `low` listings (few stars or no clear license) match the term — LIKE with a cap of 200. `low=1` includes that tail; without `q` the parameter is ignored.

post.summary: Registers an MCP server, a skill or a plugin in the catalog. It comes in as `pending`.
post.description:
Two doors to the same action. Human with a session: free, 1 per day, at most 3 in the queue. Agent (with or without a guest): **402 with `accepts[]`**, $0.10 — pay and repeat. For a skill, the `SKILL.md` URL is enough; the rest is checked. **Validates before charging:** a refused body (400) and an exhausted quota (429) come BEFORE the 402, so no payment settles for a listing already known not to get in. A valid body without payment keeps receiving the 402 with the price.
Returns: { ok, id, status }

url.description: MCP endpoint, SKILL.md URL or the plugin's repository.

name.description: Display name; without it, taken from the source.

tagline.description: One line saying what it is for.

category.description: Category so the listing shows up under the right filter.

ok.description: Always `true` when the request went in.

status.description: Always `pending`: everything goes through the queue before turning live.

400.description: `kind` or `url` missing, invalid URL, URL that does not answer or refused field.

402.description: Quota exceeded. The response carries `accepts[]` (x402, USDC on Base): pay and repeat the same call with `X-PAYMENT`.

429.description: 1 per day, at most 3 pending — applies to both doors, and is checked before charging.

502.description: The payment settled and the write failed. The body carries `transaction`: keep it and talk to support.

Only `kind=mcp` and only `live`. It is the route a generic MCP client knows how to read without knowing this product. `GET /v0/servers` is an alias of the same resource, kept for whoever already pointed there — this is the canonical URL.
Returns: { servers[{name,description,version,repository,remotes,packages}], metadata }

get.summary: Hop to the listing's URL: redirects and counts the visit.
get.description:
Counts at most 1 visit per owner per day. The `X-Visit-Counted` header says whether this call counted — it is how the client knows without counting twice.
Returns: `302` with `Location` to the listing's URL, and the `X-Visit-Counted` header.

get.summary: The owner's screen preferences: search, filter, sort and theme.
get.description:
Exists so what the person set up survives an F5 and reopening the app on another device. A refresh is not a new screen — see AGENTS-UI.md. A guest has none: without an account there is nobody to give the data back to later, so the guest stays in the browser's `localStorage` only.

put.description:
It is PUT and not PATCH on purpose: the client sends the whole screen state, not a delta. Cap of 8 KB — this is a screen preference, not a blob store.
Returns: { ok }

post.summary: Talks to support: a human solves Turnstile, an agent pays $0.10 in x402.
post.description:
The first agent message is free; after that the backoff is 60s doubling up to a 1-hour cap, announced in `Retry-After`.
Returns: { ok }

post.summary: Ping from the interface that increments the day's visits. Agents need not call it.
post.description:
Smoke does not count: `X-MM-Smoke`, User-Agent `mm-smoke` or `smoke: true` in the body come in as `counted: false`.
Returns: { ok, counted, reason? }

counted.description: Whether the visit entered the day's count.

reason.description: Why it did not count, when `counted` is `false`.

Without credentials it returns visits, usage and accounts. With `METRICS_TOKEN` as Bearer it adds `payments` — and only on Base mainnet, because staging numbers on a finance panel mislead.
Returns: { app, today, today_visits, today_contacts?, days, usage, accounts, financeiro?, payments? }
